why: Rebuild the tree from its preorder string with null markers, then visit every node and check the ones with both children: a single DFS where each node compares value + left + right against target.
hints: Preorder with # markers fully determines the tree: read a token, build the left subtree, then the right.
While rebuilding, each node knows its two direct children's values once both subtrees are read; that is when to test the sum.
Recursive (or explicit-stack) parser over the token list with a moving index; count nodes where both children exist and the three values sum to target. O(n).
pitfalls: A node with only one child never qualifies, even if value + child == target.
Strip spaces around tokens; values can be negative.
Sums reach 3 * 10^9: use 64-bit integers outside Python.
